about: Sedici for two players («il giuoco più facile ad impararsi, perchè in questo si danno poche carte», p. 15) of the Turin rulebook «Primi elementi e regole del giuoco de' tarocchi» (Torino, Soffietti, 1787), read on the scan (two readings and a check, 23 November 2026, pp. 7-46): four cards to each player (pp. 17-18, 35), dealt again and again from the same pack until a player says «fuora», which means the game is won (p. 39); a player says «fuora» when he is sure he has made sixteen points (p. 35), a false claim is paid double with fewer than eight points and simple with more (p. 39); the Fool here is an ordinary trionfo, the lowest, taken by Bagatto (pp. 14, 36, 38-39), and counts one point; the cards are counted one at a time (p. 51). A plain card counted singly is worth 1, as the Turin books of 1846 count Sedici and Trent'uno alike (Prammatica [1846], p. 12; Torino [1846], part I, p. 30; our reading, the book of 1787 prints no price); with that value the pack cannot run out before a player has sixteen, and when it does run out before anybody has said «fuora» (a player who does not see his points) the hand ends with no payment (ours; Dummett 1980, p. 269 gives this guess for Trentuno; at Sedici his guess is a further deal of four cards to each player after the first four tricks, the repeated deal this file plays). A match is a race to five points: each game won is one point, as Prammatica [1846], p. 11 says that a partita at Sedici seldom ends at the first point; the number five is our reading of p. 13. Prammatica [1846], p. 12 says that Sedici «va soggetto a quasi tutte le regole» of Trent'uno al più; where the two books differ (the Fool and Bagatto), this file follows Torino 1787. Marks: [D] documented, [R] our reading, [S] sources silent.

torino1846.cite: L. B., Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, part I (Grammatica del giuocatore), Torino, Serra, [1846]

dummett1980.cite: M. Dummett, The Game of Tarot, London, Duckworth, 1980; chapter XIII, pp. 258-279 (partial scan held, p. 268 missing)

prammatica1846.cite: L. B., Prammatica del giuocatore di tarocchi ossia regole indispensabili per gli amatori di simile passatempo, Torino, Serra, [1846] (separate issue, cover dated 1846, deposited 27 December 1845; reprinted from the same setting, same pages, as part II of Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, Torino, Serra, [1846])

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 14-15: the teacher and the reader «faremo pertanto una partita al Sedici», two players; the first deal is drawn as in the example of p. 16.

direction.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 37: «gli altri sempre a destra procedendo»: play passes to the right; with two players the direction changes nothing.

first_dealer.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 16: cards are turned up for each side, «se viene prima da questa parte un Trionfo, mischierò io»: the side that first receives a trionfo shuffles and deals first.

cut_by.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 16-17: the player on the dealer's left cuts («di dar a coppare a chi ti siede a sinistra»); if he declines the next on the left, if all decline the dealer deals as the pack lies.

cut_min.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 16: «Una carta sola non si può coppare»: the page forbids only a cut of one card; that each part keeps at least two cards is our reading.

dealer_rotation.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 42 (rule 44): «colui, cui tocca a mischiar le carte, è quegli per avventura, che abbia guadagnato»: the next dealer may happen to be the winner, so the deal is not the loser's by rule; p. 70: «tocca al compagno appresso a mischiare»: the next player deals. With two players the deal alternates. Revision 9 sets aside revision 8 B4, which stood only on the example of p. 41, where the winner himself had dealt. Other reading: the winner hands the whole pack to his companion (p. 41, «rimetterai le carte tutte in mazzo al tuo compagno»), so the loser deals.

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 39-41: each player makes his own points and the first to sixteen says «fuora»; the winner is paid by the others.

deck.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 9-10: «Settant'otto Tarocchi si richiedono»: twenty-two trionfi (the Fool is n. 0 among them) and fourteen cards in each of the four suits.

trump_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 13, 37, 38-39: the Angel XX is not taken by any («l'Angelo non è preso da alcuno», p. 37) and takes the World XXI («appresso noi prende il Mondo»), the other trionfi rank by number, and the Fool is the lowest, taken by Bagatto («viene preso assolutamente da Bagatto», p. 14); the Fool takes nothing of the trionfi (p. 38: «non prenderà mai Bagatto»). The list is highest first. Prammatica [1846], p. 12 puts the Fool above Bagatto at Trent'uno al più («egli prende Bagatto occorrendo») and Sedici follows «quasi tutte le regole» of that game; Torino [1846], part I, p. 26 has Bagatto take the Fool at Sedici. Not followed.

suit_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 11-13: in swords and batons the larger number takes the smaller; in cups and coins «la carta di numero inferiore prende quella di numero superiore, eccetto le figure» (the ace takes the two up to the ten); the courts stand above every numeral. The order among the courts is printed, pp. 11-12: «il Re bensì prende la Donna, il Cavallo, il Fante».

card_points.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 13-14, 38: king 5, queen 4, knight 3, jack 2, the Angel 5, Bagatto 5, and the Fool «conta un sol punto» at Sedici and Trent'uno; the World has no value of its own. A plain card is worth count.plain_value.

fool.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 36, 38: the Fool takes a trick as a trionfo («prende con un Trionfo qualunque siasi, con Bagatto per esempio, col Folle, coll'Angelo») and a lone Fool must be played to answer a trionfo («siamo obbligati a darlo per non rinegare»); it is not the excuse of the long games. Bagatto takes it (pp. 14, 38-39).

options.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 21 (rule 10): «quanto si giuochi la partita semplice, qualunque sia il giuoco, che facciasi»: the stake of the simple game is settled before the deal. The book names no amount (p. 15 plays «un quattrino per ciascuna partita» as an example); the list of choices is the table's.

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 39: «Seguiterai pertanto tu, che … darne quattro a … vuol dire partita guadagnata».

hand_size.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 17-18, 35: «Al giuoco del Sedici se ne danno quattro per ciascuno».

packets.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 18, 41-42: «io do tutte quattro … a due a … a tre ed una»; p. 41 adds «a tre a tre, a quattro a quattro» and «ad una e tre»: one, two, three or four at a time, three and one, one and three, as the dealer pleases.

packets_announced.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 17-18, 42: the dealer says before the cut how he will deal; whoever changes without saying so pays the simple game to all (p. 42, rule 43).

face.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 41: «quattro carte coperte prese di sopra al mazzo senza vederle».

dead.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 39, 41: «a darne quattro a tutti» again from the same pack; the cards of the earlier rounds go back into the pack only when the game is won («rimetterai le carte tutte in mazzo», p. 41). Dummett 1980, p. 269 reads it so: «without returning to the pack the cards already played». Other reading: the pack is shuffled again for each round.

first_leader.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 37 (general rule): «Colui, che or ultimo ha preso la mano ... deve essere il primo a giuocare»: each later round of the same game, after a new deal, is led by the taker of the last trick; the book does not say it for the rounds (p. 39); Dummett is silent. The first round of every game is led by the player on the dealer's right, [D] p. 35: «Chi è a destra di chi dà, comincia». Other readings: the player on the dealer's right leads every round (stood until revision 8); the last taker of the game before leads (previous_last_taker).

next_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 37: «Colui, che or ultimo ha preso la … deve essere il primo a giuocare».

follow_suit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 35: «gli altri sempre a destra procedendo debbon rispondere con carte della medesima sequenza».

must_trump.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36 prints the duty for Partita and the games after it: «si risponderà e prenderà con un Trionfo»; carried back to this game. Torino 1787, pp. 36-37, in an example «al Trent'uno, od al Sedici», plays so: «io Spade non ne tengo, metto sul tuo sette un Trionfo». Torino 1787, p. 49 (Baronetti) prints the same duty: «se non ho carte della medesima sequenza prendo con Trionfi».

must_overtrump.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 36-37: a higher trionfo takes, but the book states no duty to beat the trionfo on the table (second reading: [S]).

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 39-41: the player who has made sixteen points says «fuora» and wins. Prammatica [1846], p. 12 says of Sedici and of Trent'uno al più alike («sì nell'uno, che nell'altro», right after «Questo giuoco non differisce dal Sedici che nel numero di trent'uno») that the winner is not the one who says «fuora» first but the first to have made the points («non è già vincitore quegli che si dichiara il primo», but «il primo che è giunto a fare trent'uno»; «Chi ha vinto non può più perdere»); that is the edition of 1846; this file follows Torino 1787, where the first to say it wins, and has the other reading as the alt of `winner_is`.

target.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 35: «Per guadagnare una partita al Sedici ti basterà far sedici punti».

claim_when.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 40: «Quando adunque tu prima del tuo compagno sappi d'aver fatti sedici punti»: «fuora» is said as soon as one knows the points are made; Dummett 1980, p. 269: the first to say it wins. The table lets a player say it on any turn of his own, also in the middle of a trick (own_turn). Other readings: only right after a trick, by its taker (after_trick, stood until revision 8); at any moment, also out of turn (any_time).

at_round_end.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 39 («finchè alcuno si chiami fuora») and p. 40 («Quando adunque tu … sappi d'aver fatti sedici punti, ti dirai fuora») print that the player says «fuora» himself, when he knows he has the points; p. 46, said of Trent'uno, adds «chiamarti prontamente fuora innanzi agli altri compagni». The rule below is our reading of those lines. That is advice for winning the race: the book prints no penalty for saying it later and no duty to say it when the last trick of a packet is taken, so the next packet is dealt and the claim is made on a turn of one's own (claim_when). [S] When the pack is spent and no card will be played any more, a last window opens: each player in turn, from the taker of the last trick, says «fuora» or does not; a right claim wins, a false one is paid by the rows below, and when nobody says it the hand ends with no winner (stock_empty). The books do not mention an empty pack; the window is ours. Other reading [S]: the taker of the last trick of a packet who has the points must say «fuora» before the next deal (must_claim; played until revision 10); no book says it, ours.

winner_is.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 39-41: the player who has made sixteen points says «fuora» and wins; the first to say it wins (Dummett 1980, p. 269). Other reading [D], the edition of 1846: Prammatica [1846], p. 12, said of Sedici and of Trent'uno al più alike («sì nell'uno, che nell'altro»): «non è già vincitore quegli che si dichiara il primo», but «il primo che è giunto a fare trent'uno»; «Chi ha vinto non può più perdere». Whoever says «fuora» rightly, the game goes to the seat that made the points first. The first is the taker of the trick at which a count first reached the target.

false_claim.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 39 (rule 41): a player who says «fuora» without being out pays «la partita marcia, che vuol dir doppia, se non avrai otto punti» and, with more than eight, «sarai condannato a pagarla semplice». [R] With exactly eight points neither condition is met; read as simple. Other reading: double. To whom it is paid is not said. Paid to the opponent: [S] ours, as the general penalty of p. 38 («a tutti i giuocatori»); with two players there is one. [R] In a race (match.kind) a double row gives each other player two points, a «vada doppio», and a simple row one: Prammatica [1846], p. 13 prints the «vada doppio» for a revoke at Trent'uno al meno; carried over to the false claim, ours.

after_false_claim.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 20 (rule 9): «ma seguirassi questa sull'istesso piede»: a mistake is paid and the same game goes on; read for a false «fuora». p. 39 (rule 41) prints only the payment. Other version: a false claim loses the game, as in the Savoy «À Fora» (rules of Annecy, in Depaulis 1984).

replace.what: a false «fuora»: does the game go on or end

after_first_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 40-41: «Guadagnata la partita, deporrai le tue carte»: the game is won, the winner counts his points aloud and is paid.

stock_empty.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 39 and Torino [1846], part I, p. 26: «finchè alcuno si chiami fuora»; an empty pack is not mentioned. Ours after Dummett 1980, p. 269, who names two guesses for Trentuno: the hand is given up without payment, or all the cards are dealt again; the first is played. For Sedici the same page guesses a further deal of four cards to each player after the first four tricks, when nobody has made sixteen points: that is the repeated deal this file already plays, not a rule for an empty pack, and on an empty pack he says nothing for Sedici. With a plain card at 1 the cards dealt always carry more than fifteen points for each seat, so the pack cannot run out before somebody has sixteen; the last window is kept for a player who does not say it. Revision 1 gathered the untaken cards and dealt on, which cannot be done: too few cards are left for another round.

replace.what: the pack runs out and nobody has said «fuora»

group.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 51-52: the Sedici count is not the pair count of the long games: «E non basta per contare (come al Sedici, ed al Trent'uno) una carta sola»; at Sedici the cards are counted one at a time («per volta», p. 52).

trick_multipliers.source: [R] Torino 1787: the count is the one the section names; the book prints no trick multiplier and no war in these games (x2 and x4 are Duello's own).

last_trick_bonus.source: [R] Torino 1787: the book prints no bonus for the last trick (the +5 is Duello's own).

plain_value.source: [R] Prammatica [1846], p. 12: Trent'uno al più «non differisce dal Sedici che nel numero di trent'uno», and there the Fool «vale come semplice Tarocco» and «si conta dunque il Matto per uno, e non per cinque punti»: a plain card counts one. Torino [1846], part I, p. 30: «Tanto al Trent'uno, come al Sedici le carte si contano ad una ad una»; p. 37, «Al Sessantatre»: the same rules, 63 points to win, the Fool «come un semplice Trionfo … vale per uno e non per cinque punti». Counted one by one the pack holds 126 points, of which 63 is half. Torino 1787, pp. 13-14 and 51-52 print no value for a plain card counted singly. The Savoy «Fora» to 31 (rules of Annecy, Depaulis 1984, p. 123): «toutes les autres petites cartes pour un point». Other reading: 0, as Dummett 1980, p. 269, who writes himself that «it would be possible to suppose that they counted 1 point each»; Torino 1787, pp. 51-52: in the count by pairs a King «con una cartaccia vale 5». This file counted 0 until revision 13.

winner.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 39: «finchè alcuno si chiami fuora, che vuol dir partita guadagnata»: the first to be out wins.

game_points.source: [R] Prammatica [1846], pp. 11, 13: «Se poi a più punti si stabilisce la partita o la presa»: there «partita» is the whole match, played to several points («difficil cosa che una partita al Sedici abbia il suo termine nel primo punto»). That each game won is one point, a «vada», is our reading: the page counts in points only the penalty («perdono il punto, così detto Vada semplice»). So a game won gives its winner one point in the race of match.kind. The stake of Torino 1787, p. 41 is still paid by the settle phase.

unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 21, 41: «sarai pagato secondo fu convenuta la partita»: the winner is paid the stake agreed before the deal.

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 41: the winner «sarai pagato secondo fu convenuta la partita» by his one opponent.

amount.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 41: «secondo fu convenuta la partita»; the amount is the agreed simple game (p. 21).

kind.source: [D] Prammatica [1846], p. 11: «difficil cosa che una partita al Sedici abbia il suo termine nel primo punto»; «Se poi a più punti si stabilisce la partita o la presa»: the match is played to several points, each game won being one. The book of 1787 describes one game only. Other version, also printed (pp. 11, 13): the match «al primo vada», every game stands alone and is paid at once; then the length of a match is ours, one round of dealers (match.kind ledger with match.dealer_rounds 1).

target.source: [R] Prammatica [1846], p. 13 names the match played «a più punti non meno di cinque» in the article on Trent'uno al meno, which refers back to Sedici and Trent'uno; the page names no other number. Ours: five, the least the page allows. [S] When the leaders are level at five or more, another game is played, until one leads alone: the sources say nothing of it; other version, the match is drawn. Which custom was played, the race or «al primo vada», is open (match.kind).

replace.what: which custom was played, a race or «al primo vada», to how many points, and what is done when the leaders are level

effect.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 33-34, 38: a player who does not answer in the suit asked, or who keeps a lone Bagatto or Fool when a trionfo is led, «nella pena accennata al num. 35. di … partita a tutti i giuocatori compagni» (rule 35 lets the card be changed while the trick is still on the table). In a race (match.kind) Prammatica [1846] reads otherwise: the offender loses a point, p. 11: «perdono il punto, così detto Vada semplice»; p. 12: «Chi rinnega, strettamente parlando, perde il Vada».

[D] Torino 1787, p. 42 (rule 43): a dealer who changes his method of dealing without timely notice «sarà tenuto ... a pagar la partita semplice a tutti i compagni giuocatori»; so for a card announced one way and dealt another (p. 18).

[D] Torino 1787, pp. 18-19 (rule 5): «Pagherai similmente la partita, se darai giuoco … carta di più, o di meno»; p. 19 (rule 6): if the fault is found at the end the dealer «pagherai d'obbligazione tutti i giuocatori» and «lascierai correr la mano al tuo compagno a destra»: he pays every other player and the deal passes to the right. [R] The redeal (hand: redeal) is our reading: the book prints the payment, not a new deal of the same hand.

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 44 (rule 46): a player who says «Avete rifiutato, o rinegato» may not see the revoke until the game is quite over, but watches that the offender does not mix the cards of his points; nobody may ever mix the covered cards on the table, even his own, on pain of paying «la partita dell'Onoranza».
left_out.why: The engine bars an illegal card, so no claim arises.
